purpose: Teach: 年長/憤り/カンタン/逝っ/ねらっ/まっか/他界/対極

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが年長の方々を敬われた
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, Dad had such respect for his elders.
lines.style: Soft, nostalgic opening. Quiet reverence in the voice. Measured pace, as if watching a memory from a distance. Gentle trailing-off—not quite finished with the thought.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: うん、お祖父ちゃん、不正に憤りを感じる方だったわよね、あなた?
lines.en: Yes, he was the type to get angry at injustice, wasn't he, dear?
lines.style: Warm agreement, gently prompting. A knowing nod in the voice. Tender but present—the rhythm of a long marriage asking and answering together.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが「カンタンには折れない」と仰った
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, Dad used to say he wouldn't break easily.
lines.style: Quiet pride underneath the wistfulness. Weight on the words 「折れない」—admiration and something protected. Slight pause before continuing, holding the memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、ご友人が次々と逝ってしまわれて寂しがってらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: He got lonely after his friends started passing, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Gentle observation, softer now. Not a question really—a recognition. Her voice carries the weight of understanding without dwelling on it. Compassionate baseline.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんが鶏をねらって撮影された
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, Dad used to photograph the chickens.
lines.style: A small smile in the voice—a shift to something lighter. Still wistful but touched with affection for the detail. Slower, more intimate pace. Settling into a quieter memory.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、お酒で顔がまっかになられたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: He'd get so red in the face after a drink, didn't he, dear?
lines.style: Tender amusement now. A slight laugh in her voice—not mocking, but loving. The warmth of a woman who found her husband endearing in his small absurdities. Light and easy.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ばあさん、若い頃、お父さんのご友人が他界された
lines.en: Gran, when he was young, one of Dad's friends passed away.
lines.style: The wistfulness deepens. A minor key in the voice—sorrow without self-pity. Careful articulation, respect for the weight of loss. Quieter still than before.

lines.speaker: sachiko_grandma
lines.jp: お祖父ちゃん、私とは対極の性格でいらしたわよね、あなた?
lines.en: He was so different from me in temperament, wasn't he, dear?
lines.style: Close, intimate delivery. Almost a whisper—sharing a secret observation only they would understand. Tender without sentimentality. The acceptance of a lifelong partnership.
